name: Vocabulary Diversity Analysis
description: Evaluates the richness and variety of the vocabulary deployed throughout a text. Large Language Models operate on probability distributions that inherently favor high-frequency, safe word choices. To maintain coherence and minimize 'perplexity' (surprise), an AI will frequently recycle a narrow band of 'optimal' words rather than foraging for diverse synonyms. In contrast, human writers—driven by stylistic flair, memory recall quirks, or the desire to avoid redundancy—naturally inject a much wider, often suboptimal (from a pure probability standpoint) variety of unique words into their prose. This algorithm detects the mathematical signature of an artificially constrained, highly recycled vocabulary.
algorithm: Lexical Richness Metrics (MTLD, HD-D, and TTR)
mechanism: The algorithm computes multiple indices of vocabulary diversity. It starts with the basic Type-Token Ratio (TTR, the ratio of unique words to total words), but heavily relies on length-agnostic measurements like the Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD) and the Hypergeometric Distribution D (HD-D / vocd-D). These advanced metrics calculate how fast the TTR drops as the text gets longer, or compute the probability of finding new words in random textual samples. Text that exhibits a statistically abnormal lack of unique word variations—reusing the same descriptive adjectives, transition phrases, and verbs where a human would organically diversify—triggers a high artificiality score.
useCase: Crucial for analyzing essays, creative writing, and extended articles. It is highly effective at identifying text that 'sounds smart' but is actually repeating a very small pool of sophisticated words.
strengths:
• Highly resilient against simple 'paraphrase' prompts; an AI instructed to 'use different words' will still draw from its constrained high-probability pool, failing to achieve true human-like lexical diversity.
• The use of MTLD and HD-D makes this analysis robust against variations in document length, unlike basic TTR.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing highly technical documentation, legal contracts, or scientific papers where strict adherence to standardized terminology (and avoidance of synonyms) is required.
• Requires a minimum text length (usually >150 words) to calculate statistically significant HD-D and MTLD scores.
parameters:
Analysis: Lexical Variation and Synonym Foraging
Metrics: MTLD (Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity) & HD-D
Output: 0-100 Lexical Repetitiveness Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-82% accuracy. It is a powerful syntactic diagnostic tool, especially when combined with burstiness and semantic coherence metrics, as LLMs struggle to simultaneously optimize for coherence and true lexical diversity.

references.title: McCarthy, P. M., & Jarvis, S. (2010). MTLD, vocd-D, and HD-D: A validation study of sophisticated approaches to lexical diversity assessment. Behavior Research Methods.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
